In this VladTV interview, Charleston White revisits the summer he says changed his life: running away from home in Fort Worth, Texas, carrying a .25 pistol as a young teen, and firing after two white men outside a Pizza Inn allegedly used the N-word over a car dispute. White details the moments around Arkansas and Collins, the dollar movies, Taco Bell crowds, juvenile detention, probation under Officer Kelly Willis, and how the incident came just before the murder case that sent him into the juvenile system.

The conversation expands into youth crime, accountability, gang influence, Tarrant County courts, and the 1990s “super predator” era. Vlad fact-checks references to Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden’s Senate remarks, the crime bill debate, and later reform efforts tied to Donald Trump. White reflects on trauma, disability, fitting in with older kids, and why juvenile justice remains a major topic today.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/8YYmtZYQ0Aw
--------
In this VladTV conversation, DJ Vlad asks Robinhood co-founder and CEO Vlad Tenev how a scrappy fintech startup raised its earliest checks before major Silicon Valley backing arrived. Tenev recalls taking $50,000 and $100,000 investments through AngelList at a $10 million valuation cap, pitching everyday investors — even people in Iowa — alongside firms like Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins and Andreessen Horowitz. With Robinhood’s market cap cited at $103 billion, he says some seed backers who held through the 2022 downturn may have turned initial stakes into nine-figure gains.

The discussion expands to Robinhood Ventures, IPO Access and public-market access to startup investing through funds like RB1 and RB2, with exposure to companies such as OpenAI, Stripe and Y Combinator startups. DJ Vlad also discusses investing in Jeff Bezos’ Project Prometheus and Amazon, while Tenev critiques accreditation rules that allow meme coins but restrict access to private companies like Anthropic and SpaceX.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Vincent “Gigi” Marino reflects on serving a 28-year federal prison sentence and explains the unwritten rules that govern life inside penitentiaries. Marino discusses why “good paperwork,” respect, paying debts, and minding your business can determine whether someone survives, especially for informants and sex offenders. He also addresses the reality of prison rape, saying it is rarer than many believe, while alleging that correctional officers sometimes create dangerous situations by placing vulnerable inmates with known predators.

Marino breaks down prison politics by race, region, and affiliation, including Boston and Italian crews, New York alliances, the Aryan Brotherhood, Mexican Mafia factions from Texas and California, Paisas, Bloods, and Crips. He also describes how violence escalates in federal penitentiaries, explaining why inmates may carry multiple knives and admitting he once stabbed someone over disrespect.

Irving challenges the reliability of political polling, pointing back to Hillary Clinton’s 2016 numbers, while arguing that everyday signs—gas prices, grocery stores, and public frustration—tell a different story. The conversation moves into distrust of government, voter power, and the sense that American politics has become “a big TV show.” Prez and Irving also discuss possible future figures like Gavin Newsom and Kamala Harris, rising interest in socialism, and names like Mamdani as voters search for something different. From Michigan to national politics, the debate captures a growing demand for change, uncertainty, and what Irving calls “true freedom.”

recentItems.title: Cody Alford on Wanting to Take His Own Life After Leaving Marines (Part 6)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 5: https://youtu.be/KnkDVhbgM2A
Part 1: https://youtu.be/ORHsx5EqZJM
--------
Former Marine Cody Alford sits down with Vlad to discuss leaving the military after 15 years and seven months, the toll of traumatic brain injuries, and the mental health crisis he faced after the 2006 Still Curtain deployment and the death of his friend Jon Longoria. Alford opens up about seeking help at a Naval Hospital in Oceanside, California, the stigma around suicide prevention in elite units like Force Reconnaissance, and how medication impacted his performance.

He also explains how, before retirement, he pursued experimental brain treatment in Tampa, Florida, then sold his belongings with his wife, built out a Dodge ProMaster van, and traveled the United States with no set plan. Alford reflects on starting a YouTube channel, losing identity after service, therapy, psychedelics, DD214 transition struggles, leadership, war, and helping veterans ask for support without fear.

--------
Poetik Flakko joins DJ Vlad for a sharp VladTV discussion connecting hip-hop interviews, legal exposure, and the fallout from Vlad’s lawsuit against Aries Spears over an alleged unauthorized video. The conversation shifts to Keefe D, the Tupac Shakur murder case, and how statements made in books, podcasts, and interviews can resurface in court. Vlad explains how Keefe D’s Amazon book and past interview comments were referenced during legal proceedings, while Flakko argues the case is a warning about self-incrimination and underestimating circumstantial evidence. They also debate Las Vegas, Compton street politics, Suge Knight declining to testify, and lingering questions around Biggie Smalls, Diddy rumors, and Erich “Von Zip” Martin. A candid look at media, accountability, and the legal risks facing hip-hop figures.
